video_title: Why Agents Love Supabase — with Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson
gist: Latent Space interviews Supabase co-founders Paul Copplestone and Ant Wilson ahead of Supabase Select: ~5M databases launched monthly, a revenue target hit in four months, rising conversion from agent-driven signups, and launches of Supabase Compute, OrioleDB (Apache 2), Multigres, and the Turso acquisition to scale to billions of databases. They detail a control-group sales comp model, a greenfield-only enterprise strategy, CPU scarcity pushing multi-cloud via CapitalG/GCP, and ~$300K/month AI spend for ~450 staff.

themes.theme: Supabase growth driven by AI agents

insights.claim: The host says Supabase went from zero to about a $10B valuation in six years as a fully remote open-source company and is becoming the standard for hosting Postgres.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Supabase is a leading private infrastructure beneficiary of AI coding.

insights.claim: Supabase launches about 5 million databases per month and expects to need billions per month, driven by non-technical builders and AI agents.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Database creation is scaling with agentic app building, requiring new architectures.
insights.quote: At the moment we launch about 5 million databases on our platform every single month.

insights.claim: Supabase describes three AI chapters: embeddings via pgvector-style Postgres vectors, the vibe-coding wave (Lovable, Bolt) from end-2024, and a 2026 surge as models improved, with top-of-funnel signups rising rapidly on minimal marketing spend.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Each AI wave compounded Supabase's developer funnel.

insights.claim: Supabase says that unusually, as consumer-like agent-driven traffic surged, activation and paid conversion both rose, because agents perform signup-to-activation in one step (near 100%) and those users convert better than traditional developers.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Agent-driven users can be higher quality than human developer signups.
insights.quote: the sign up to activation, the agent does it for you.

insights.claim: Supabase set an ambitious annual revenue target at its start-of-year offsite and hit it in about four months.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: 2026 growth has dramatically exceeded internal plans.
insights.quote: it took us like 4 months to hit the number.

insights.claim: Supabase says AI lifted its product-led growth ceiling, previously estimated at $100-200M, to an unknown level potentially in the billions.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: PLG infrastructure companies may scale far beyond historic norms.

insights.claim: Supabase says it has seen customers generating serious cash within the same week of starting a project, e.g., ~$10,000 in the first few days, by adding Stripe at the agentic layer.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Time-to-revenue for new apps has collapsed.

insights.claim: The host's AEO tracker shows every frontier model recommends Supabase as its primary integrated backend; founders attribute this to being in market 3-4 years before LLMs plus heavy community content that was absorbed into training.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Pre-LLM community content created a durable 'answer engine' moat.

insights.claim: Supabase says about 60% of every YC batch uses Supabase, and it models itself on Stripe in retaining developer love while moving upmarket.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Startup mindshare is the funnel for later enterprise expansion.
insights.quote: we have 60% of every YC batch use superbase.

themes.theme: Product announcements: compute, OrioleDB, Multigres, Turso

insights.claim: Supabase Compute launches long-running, serverless, container-style compute colocated on the database's private network, removing Edge Functions' limits (Deno-based) and enabling Rust, Python and agents.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Supabase is expanding from database to full agentic backend and durable workflows.

insights.claim: OrioleDB, a drop-in Postgres storage engine replacing heap, runs about 1.5-2x faster, removes the need for vacuum, is entering full beta, and has been released under Apache 2 including a patent Supabase acquired.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Open-sourcing a patented engine strengthens Postgres ecosystem lock-in to Supabase.

insights.claim: Supabase found every existing Postgres operator could lose data under certain conditions, so it rewrote the operator layer as Multigres, which passed 1,000 sequential failovers with no data loss.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Reliability gaps in Postgres clustering are a competitive opening.
insights.quote: under um certain conditions every single one of them could lose data

insights.claim: Multigres, led by Vitess creator Sugu, prioritizes compatibility so sharding (expected around early next year) will require zero application code changes; design partners include Booz Allen, Postman and Perplexity.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Transparent Postgres sharding could pull large workloads from MySQL.

insights.claim: Supabase announced acquiring Turso, which built multi-writer MVCC on a SQLite fork, to power a new small 'Supabase Spark' instance type with a pathway to Postgres compatibility and upgrade to full Postgres and Multigres.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: File-format databases are the route to billions of tiny agent-created databases.

insights.claim: The founders say chatbot platforms like ChatGPT (~1.2 billion MAU) would need billions of databases monthly to default to Supabase, which it couldn't serve until the Turso acquisition.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Default-provider deals with frontier labs are gated by scale-out capability.

insights.claim: Supabase's latest step for declarative schemas (PG Delta library) represents the full Postgres shape in files, since agents can't efficiently infer schema from a thousand migration files.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Git-native, declarative infrastructure is key for agent usability.

insights.claim: Supabase says innovations from object storage (S3 strong consistency, S3 Express with ~1-2ms writes) let databases be built on object storage, good for small use cases but not massive transactional scale.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Object storage is reshaping database architecture at the small end.

insights.claim: Supabase believes sharding is the best way to scale OLTP to petabytes and that analytics should be handled separately (interest in DuckDB/DuckLake) rather than chasing HTAP.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Supabase won't compete directly in unified HTAP.

insights.claim: Supabase says it repeatedly hits capacity runways and meets AWS multiple times, paying more for compute amid a CPU shortage.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: CPU scarcity is a binding constraint for fast-growing infra companies.

insights.claim: Supabase is bringing on CapitalG as an investor for access to the Alphabet ecosystem and GCP, moving to a multi-cloud strategy for more compute.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Compute access is now a factor in choosing investors.

insights.claim: The host notes DigitalOcean is now worth about $16B after compute prices tripled in the last year; DigitalOcean lost Supabase to AWS early by refusing YC credits.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Compute scarcity has re-rated smaller cloud providers.

insights.claim: Supabase's sales model uses product triggers: of ~1,000 weekly triggered emails, non-responders (a control group) grow 25% month-over-month while those getting a help call grow 125%, and reps are paid only on the 100% incremental uplift.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Measuring sales by incremental uplift vs a control group is a replicable PLG sales design.

insights.claim: Supabase says enterprise database migrations almost never happen, so it focuses on winning greenfield workloads on day one and will not make migrations a core focus for ~5 years.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Database share is won at creation, not by displacement.
insights.quote: I guarantee they'll almost never migrate.

insights.claim: Supabase says only about 5% of Oracle workloads by revenue ran in the cloud as of a year ago, but ripping out Oracle is incredibly difficult due to OLTP downtime and split-brain risk.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Legacy Oracle displacement remains slow despite coding agents.

insights.claim: Supabase is launching Control Tower, a repackaging of Supabase for Platforms that lets enterprises monitor and administer fleets of internal Supabase instances.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Enterprise fleet management turns bottom-up adoption into enterprise contracts.

insights.claim: Supabase now sees C-level champions such as CPOs who hadn't coded in 10 years building internal tools with Lovable and Supabase.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: AI coding creates executive-level buyers for dev infrastructure.

insights.claim: Supabase argues databases are stickier than front-end tools like Lovable because running databases is hard and migrating a database is harder than switching front ends.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Backend infra captures more durable value than app builders.

themes.theme: AI spend, open source and org design

insights.claim: Supabase spends about $300K per month on AI tokens for ~450 employees.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Benchmark of roughly $650 per employee per month in AI spend.
insights.quote: So currently we spend about 300k per month.

insights.claim: The host proposes a token-to-salary ratio metric: many companies are at ~0.1, up to 1.0 is safe, and over 1.5 is likely trouble; the 50th-percentile OpenAI employee spends ~$3-5K/month.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: A simple benchmark for managing enterprise AI coding budgets.

insights.claim: Supabase is earmarking about $1 million of stock to give to community members, starting with Gary Abbott, who answered ~20,000 Discord questions in six years, 13,000 within an hour.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Equity-for-community models bypass accredited-investor limits.

insights.claim: Supabase predicts most open-source tools will be rewritten (likely in Rust) once, with a few winners per category, rather than everything being continuously re-vibe-coded.
insights.speaker: Supabase co-founder
insights.so_what: Open-source consolidation into safer languages is coming.

insights.claim: The host says AI SRE remains one of the hardest categories for agent startups, and Supabase is hiring SREs most urgently among ~50 open roles.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Operations/reliability remains a human bottleneck.
